notes.title: New Compression System + .NET 10 Preview
notes.content:
[b]We’ve deployed a major update to the Anti-Extinction launcher system — introducing NessiePreLoader, our new runtime management tool.[/b]

This update streamlines future upgrades by safely handling .NET transitions, executable replacements, and launcher validation — all without user disruption.

[h2]⚙️ What Is NessiePreLoader?[/h2]
[list]
[*] A transitional bootstrapper built with .NET Framework 4.8
[*] Executes from a temporary, isolated user directory to avoid file locks
[*] Detects and removes outdated runtime previews
[*] Installs .NET 10 Preview 4 components
[*] Verifies all file hashes using SHA256 before proceeding
[*] Replaces the original launcher with the updated .NET 10 version
[*] Cleans up after itself to leave no trace
[/list]

[h2] What Happened During This Update[/h2]
[list]
[*] NessiePreLoader launched from a secure temporary environment
[*] Detected that .NET 10 Preview 4 was not installed
[*] Identified and attempted cleanup of .NET 10 Preview 3 remnants
[*] Verified local installer file integrity using SHA256 hashing
[*] Installed both the .NET Runtime and Windows Desktop Runtime
[*] Located and validated KaikoAetherLauncher.zip
[*] Extracted 17 files into the game installation directory
[/list]

[h2] Executable Handoff Completed[/h2]
[list]
[*] Backed up the original .NET Framework launcher to a safe location
[*] Renamed Pre_Anti-Extinction.exe to Anti-Extinction.exe
[*] Launched the new .NET 10 executable
[*] Performed full self-cleanup of temp files and stubs
[/list]

[h2] Safety, Stability & Transparency[/h2]
[list]
[*] All installer files passed SHA256 hash verification
[*] All operations were timestamp-logged for traceability
[*] Runtime checks were attempted post-install for extra safety
[*] Installation continued safely even when some registry keys weren't found
[*] Final status: [b]All steps completed successfully[/b]
[/list]

[h2] Summary[/h2]
[list]
[*] NessiePreLoader is now part of our core update infrastructure
[*] Anti-Extinction now runs on .NET 10 Preview 4
[*] Future updates, patches, and transitions will be handled smoothly
[*] No user input, launcher restart, or external tools required
[/list]

notes.title: Vulkan Freezing Issue – Community Help Needed
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We’re currently tracking a critical Vulkan rendering issue affecting Standalone builds in Unity, and we need your help to gather data and push for a fix!

🔍 Issue Overview:
Vulkan rendering freezes after 1-10 seconds, but game logic (audio, input) keeps running.
DX11 & DX12 work fine, and Vulkan works fine inside the Unity Editor—but breaks in Standalone.
RTX 3060 requires launching another Vulkan game first for it to work.
RTX 3070 Ti consistently freezes in Standalone, no matter the driver.
RTX 4070 Super works fine with Vulkan out of the box.
📌 How You Can Help!
✅ Run the game using Vulkan and report any freezes, crashes, or weird behavior.
✅ Test different NVIDIA driver versions and let us know if rolling back fixes anything.
✅ Try launching another Vulkan game first, then run our game to see if it makes a difference.
✅ Submit your logs and findings in our community server!

📥 Where to Submit Your Reports:
Join our Discord server and DM me your logs!

🔗 Join Here: discord.gg/furr-tec

Your help is hugely appreciated—the more reports we get, the faster we can get this fixed with Unity and NVIDIA! Let’s solve this together! 💪🚀

notes.title: MAW Dynamics part 1
notes.content:
[h1]What’s New in Anti-Extinction RC? Oh, Just Everything.
[/h1]

1. 🌀 Maw Dynamics (Part 1 of 2) is Finally Here!

This is our brand-new chaos destruction engine, and it’s like nothing you’ve experienced before. Imagine sound waves inside a game behaving exactly like they do in real life—echoes bouncing off walls, bass resonating through objects, and the world reacting in real-time to destruction.
Think of it as Horizon’s destruction engine meets sound acoustics simulation—a perfect blend of chaos and realism. With Maw Dynamics, explosions don’t just look good—they sound like they’re breaking the sound barrier!

2. Unity 6000.1.a9 Upgrade!

Yep, we’re now running on Unity 6.1 Alpha 9! Why stick with 6.1 Alpha 7 when we can push even further into the future?

[b]Some highlights from this shiny new upgrade:
[/b]
[list] 
[*] Improved physics simulation (perfect for making Maw Dynamics even crazier).
[*] Rendering pipeline optimizations—because who doesn’t want prettier graphics and smoother performance?

Better editor performance—so our devs can spend less time waiting for progress bars and more time breaking (and fixing) things.

Enhanced shader support for crafting visuals so crisp, you’ll think your monitor is 4D.

What Does This Mean for You?

Destruction That Feels Alive: Whether it’s a building collapsing or a small object shattering, you’re not just seeing it—you’re hearing the world respond as if you’re really there.

[*]Smooth Performance, No Matter Your Rig: Potato PCs, rejoice! And for you hardware enthusiasts out there, your supercomputer will finally get the workout it deserves.

Even Prettier Worlds: Our visuals are leveling up so hard, you’ll wonder if you’re still playing a game or living in the future.
Stay Tuned for More!

Maw Dynamics is just getting started—Part 2 will blow your mind (and probably your speakers). We’ve got even more features cooking up, and trust me, they’re going to make this game the talk of 2025.

Keep being awesome, and remember: in Anti-Extinction, the only thing going extinct is boring gameplay!


– Aether & the Furr-Tec Dev Team

notes.title: Feedback on moving to Unreal
notes.content:
I hope you're all doing well! I wanted to share some thoughts and get your feedback on a significant decision we're considering for Anti-Extinction. Due to ongoing issues and lack of support from Unity, we're contemplating a gradual transition from Unity to Unreal Engine. Below is a detailed list of the problems we've been facing:

[b]Core Issues[/b]:
[b]Unstable Editor[/b]: Basic features frequently crash the entire editor window.

[b]SRP (Scriptable Render Pipeline) Issues[/b]: Beyond my control and Unity is not addressing them.

[b]PhysX Problems[/b]: The update from 4.3.1.X to higher versions is causing severe issues with the physics system, which is crucial for Anti-Extinction. Check out the discussions here:
[b]Stuttering Issue[/b] (https://issuetracker.unity3d.com/issues/a-1000-times-heavier-gameobject-will-stutter-when-colliding-with-a-lighter-gameobject)

[b]Physics Performance Regression[/b] (https://forum.unity.com/threads/physics-performance-regression-in-unity-2022-3-8-and-onwards.1495442/#post-9675257)

[b]Garbage Editor Reload[/b]: The editor reload process is inefficient and problematic.

[b].NET 8 Delay[/b]: The absence of .NET 8 means ongoing instability and long waits for editor repaint windows.

[b]Cinemachine Issues[/b]: Working around editor issues, particularly with Cinemachine 3, causes memcpy crashes. Cinemachine 2 is stable but crashes upon updating due to a .TSS file issue.

[b]Potential Benefits of Unreal Engine[/b]:
[b]Stability[/b]: Unreal Engine 5.4 offers more stability and robust features, which could save us time and resources in the long run.
[b]Support[/b]: We can apply for Epic MegaGrants, which could provide the funding we desperately need.

[b]Important Milestones[/b]:
Q3 2024 Demo Release: We plan to release a demo of the game based on the story lore in Q3 2024. This demo will be developed in Unity to ensure we meet our timeline and provide you with a taste of what’s to come.

[b]Transition to Unreal Engine[/b]: After the demo release, we will transition to Unreal Engine to finish the work we started with Furr-Tec from 2022 to now. This move aims to enhance stability and leverage Unreal’s robust features for the final game development stages.

[b]Our Commitment to Quality[/b]
As a dev team, we want to ensure the game is as optimized and bug-free as possible for our consumers. This transition is part of our commitment to delivering the best possible experience. We believe Unreal Engine will help us achieve these goals by providing a more stable and powerful development environment.

[b]Your Feedback[/b]
We understand this is a significant shift, and we want to ensure it aligns with the expectations and support of our community. Here’s what we’re considering:
Gradual Transition: Slowly moving parts of the project to Unreal Engine while continuing some development in Unity to maintain progress and stability.
Community Involvement: Keeping you all updated on our progress and involving you in testing and feedback to ensure the transition improves the game's quality.

We value your thoughts and would love to hear your feedback on this potential transition. Do you think this move is the right step for Anti-Extinction? How do you feel about the potential benefits versus the challenges of such a transition?

Please share your thoughts and questions here

notes.title: Space exploration testing Available!
notes.content:
[b]What's new[/b]

- Physics-based spaceship controller

- Camera system comes with cockpit and third person perspectives

- Weapons and loadout system provides a variety of weapons including projectile guns, laser weapons, homing missiles, and turrets, with a comprehensive loadout system

- Radar system built for performance and efficiency, including target boxes, lead target indicators, 2D/3D radar, target selection (Next, Nearest, Front), target hologram and more. 

- Health and damage system enables individual subsystem targeting and damage, and includes energy shields, slow ship detonation (for those big capital ship explosions!), 

- Resource system for adding boost fuel consumption, ammunition and energy usage, heat production and other resource-driven gameplay mechanics. 

- Spaceship AI system includes obstacle avoidance, patrolling (between custom waypoints), formation flying, and combat (including attacking and evading) for space fighters and capital ships.


- Floating Origin System to handle large space scenes with no fuss.


- Objectives system to set up objectives for the player to complete, display them on the UI, and set up waypoints to them.


- Ship Enter/Exit System to easily enter and exit spaceships during gameplay

- Rumble system to add camera shakes and gamepad rumbles.

- Vehicle/Module system provides a strong foundation for adding functionality and modules to your ships that can be swapped out during loadout or gameplay.

Runs on Unity 6 beta 12

notes.title: What to see in Update 3
notes.content:
[i]In the wake of Ubisoft and other publishers/game makers, making AAA Titles Online only functionality is predatory behavior, learn more here[/i] [url=https://www.ubisoft.com/en-us/game/the-crew/the-crew/news-updates/mOR3tviszkxfeQCUKxhOV]ReadMore[/url]

Furr-Tec Studio’s Commitment to game preservation and Online functionality.

I.	We at Furr-Tec Studio would like to share some insights on what we plan to do to preserve our game and any future games we release.

II.	All server functionality can be locally hosted via a server manager (anti-extinction headless mode)

III.	We will provide docker containers to host an online server, meaning if we ever shut down online server hosting due to the rising cost of infrastructure, the game will be able to still work for the MMO part, not just single-player, we will make these changes early on in development so you can rest assure Anti-Extinction remains working no matter what.

IV.	We will release patches to address bugs we didn’t detect from testing, so rest assured patching of game code will remain a priority

V.	Since the start of development, the scalability of servers shouldn’t be an issue, thanks to DOTS Technology we should be able to make this run on older-gen CPUs preserving them a bit longer, (Anti-Extinction Headless Mode | Server Mode basically)

Now that, that is all taken care of, let's discuss what’s new, changed, etc.

[b]A.C.E. (Ather Chaos Engine)
[/b]
We introduced a new version of Unity, this is 2023.3.0a18 (a referring to Alpha), this has a bunch of upcoming features and QoL updates for us developers with the approaching Unity 6 LTS.

We added support and implemented NVIDIA DLSS 3, and AMD FSR 2. We also enabled a feature in Unity introduced in 2023.3.X called Batch Render Group API, which does some pretty neat stuff (this lets us perform customizable high-performance rendering).

As of right now this isn’t active *Batch Render Group* we need to do a bit more testing before we are comfortable enabling this for everyone, but it’s there! We are working on it, so it’s only a matter of time before A.C.R. gets this coded in for our Rendering, then it’s game time :3

Along with those NVIDIA/AMD Upscaling technologies we enabled STP (Scalable Temporal Post-Processing)

[b]What’s STP?[/b]
•	Scalable Temporal Post-Processing (STP) uses spatial and temporal up-sampling techniques to produce a high-quality, anti-aliased image.
•	Similar to the TAA Upscale filter, you can only use STP with the TAA anti-aliasing method. It is not compatible with other anti-aliasing methods. It also runs when you set HDRP or URP to use a 100% scale to perform anti-aliasing.
•	A limitation to using STP, is that it cannot support dynamic resolution without hardware support. You can still use it for fixed-resolution scaling in cases where hardware support is unavailable. However, the resolution scale value must be forced to a fixed percentage.
New Features Additions:
•	Maw Dynamics, full-fledged chaos physics for world destruction
•	Le Goob: we renamed it from Ardy Quadrium Interconnect, a multiplayer solution powered by DOTS Technology!
•	Small mesh culling: a new feature in Unity 2023.3.X (This is basically inserting an automatic LOD group so that when the object is below a certain screen percentage size it will be culled)
•	GPU Resident Drawer: In the latest 2023.3 alpha, Unity has added a new rendering system which is called the GPU Resident Drawer. This is a ‘behind the curtain’, GPU driven, system that allows us to author game objects and when processed they will be ingested and rendered via a special fast path that handles better instancing

The GPU resident drawer is supported on the modern rendering backends within Unity - specifically anywhere compute shaders are enabled this functionality should work. When you are running on a platform that does not meet the required hardware capabilities the rendering will fall back to the traditional, non-GPU, pathway

You can learn more here about what’s new in Unity 2023.3.X https://forum.unity.com/threads/gpu-driven-rendering-in-unity.1502702/

This upgrade from Unity 2023.2 to 2023.3 marks a pivotal moment for Anti-Extinction, bringing a host of new features and optimizations that will take your gaming adventures to unprecedented heights.

[b]Unity 2023.3: Unveiling the Powerhouse[/b]
Unity 2023.3 is not just an incremental update; it's a powerhouse of innovation and performance. Here's a glimpse into why we've chosen Unity 2023.3 for Anti-Extinction Update 3:

[b]Enhanced Graphics Performance:[/b]

The integration of Render Graph into URP empowers us to offer improved graphic performance. This allows for more advanced and customizable rendering, providing a unique visual style without tweaking the URP source code.

[b]API Access and Customizability:[/b]

Unity 2023.3 refines API access and customizability in URP, addressing complexities in creating custom post-processing effects and improving resource access. This means more control in your hands to shape the visual identity of Anti-Extinction.

[b]Artist Workflows at Their Best:[/b]

Improved graphics features translate into enhanced artist workflows. Mipmap streaming debug views, Shader Graph enhancements, and better support for VFX Graph in URP are just some of the ways we're making it easier for us to create stunning visuals.

[b]Consolidating DOTS Entity Component System (ECS) Foundations:[/b]

Unity 2023.3 continues to build on the success of Unity 2022 LTS, ensuring a powerful foundation for ambitious projects. With quicker iteration times, clearer documentation, enhanced performance, and new APIs for faster entity creation, the experience gets even better.

[b]What Does This Mean for You?[/b]

For our dedicated agents, this update represents not just a technical improvement but a promise of a more immersive and visually stunning Anti-Extinction experience. Unity 2023.3 ensures that we stay at the forefront of technology, providing you with a gaming environment that is not only cutting-edge but also fully optimized for performance.

Stay tuned for more updates as we prepare to roll out Anti-Extinction Update 3. We appreciate your unwavering support and can't wait for you to dive into the enhanced world of Anti-Extinction.

[b][u]Update 3 Releases in 2024 January[/u][/b]

notes.title: Partial-Full Release Dev Keynote
notes.content:
We're thrilled to bring you the latest update on "Anti-Extinction" and its journey to Steam. Here’s the scoop:

[b]Major Milestone Achieved!
[/b]Game Submission for Steam Review: Big news! We've officially pushed the actual game of "Anti-Extinction," not just the beta, to Steam for review. This will allow you to see the storage page of the game, the game itself is not fully released, that is scheduled for 2026

[b]Current Status[/b]: As the game is currently under review by Steam, the play tester sign-up isn’t available just yet. But don't worry, we're on the edge of our seats too, and we'll make sure you're the first to know once it's live!

[b]What's Next[/b]?
Awaiting Approval: We're eagerly awaiting the green light from Steam. This approval is crucial as it paves the way for you all to dive into the world of "Anti-Extinction."

Please keep your expectations realistic and in line with the early-access nature of this game. Your feedback and support during this pre-alpha phase are invaluable to us. Together, we can shape "Anti-Extinction" into a game that truly resonates with the furry community and beyond.


[b]Play Tester Phase[/b]: Once we have the approval, we will open up for play tester sign-ups. This phase is all about you helping us polish and perfect the game. Your feedback will be instrumental in ensuring "Anti-Extinction" is everything we've dreamed of and more.

[b]Looking Ahead to Q3 2024[/b]: Remember, after the play test phase, we're aiming for a soft open-alpha launch in Q3 2024. More testing, more feedback, and more fine-tuning to make "Anti-Extinction" a stellar experience.

[b]Stay Connected[/b]
We understand the anticipation and excitement around the game and we share it wholeheartedly. Stay tuned to our Steam page and community channels for the latest updates and announcements.

Thank you for your unwavering support and patience. It's a journey we're proud to be on with such a passionate community. We're almost there, and the adventure is just beginning!
